title: graphics switching, sharper seat view, the HUD off the wheel, smoother arms, and sleek high-tech touch controls
lensAText: a sceptical game UX designer and performance engineer. Look at every frame and the timing table the builder cites, then check it yourself in ONE short Playwright script on dist/artifact.html at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3, isMobile, hasTouch, Chrome DevTools Protocol Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4) and 1450x767: open the settings while driving and switch the graphics mode Low -> HD -> Ultra -> Low twice, plus every other setting that takes noticeable time; time each from the tap to a settled frame; check the overlay appears only when the work is noticeable, its bar fills from real progress (never jumps back, reaches 100 %, then goes), the game stays safe underneath, nothing flickers, breaks or leaks (heap after 10 switches), and the result looks the same as before. Judge: is switching clearly quicker, and does the loading display feel polished and honest? ALSO: reproduce the owner's screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/seat-view-v15-phone.webp (OC Hypercar, seat view, 969x547 phone landscape, DPR 3) and judge whether the seat view now looks sharp and smooth (no jagged edges, faceted silhouettes or soft image) and whether the wheel's centre and the cluster are clear of every HUD box. Check the arms and hands too: smooth silhouettes on the phone tier, no dark patches, the grip and thumbs exactly as before while steering to full lock. ALSO judge the touch controls against the owner's screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/touch-controls-v15-phone.png: are GAS, BRAKE, STEER and the ability buttons clearly sleeker, bolder and more high-tech, still easy to hit and read with a thumb, never covering the wheel or cluster? Is the Thrust control now uncluttered (tank on or around the button, the ability button spaced apart, nothing stacked over the wheel)?
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~6 PM PT): "make it quicker to switch between graphics mode and have like a loading display with a status bar fill up in the meantime of switching between graphics, settings, etc. when a relatively decent amount of time will be needed to apply". HEAD is the live game (local/live-preview) this worktree was created from. (1) MEASURE FIRST: every setting in the main game that triggers work (the graphics mode/quality tiers, resolution or render scale, shadows, effects, view distance, traffic density, HUD style, car change in the garage, anything else you find), the time from the tap to a settled frame on the phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, CDP CPU throttle 4) and on desktop 1280x720, and WHY each slow one is slow (shader compiles, geometry or texture rebuilds, reflection cube bakes, shadow map reallocation, world or chunk rebuilds, a page reload). (2) MAKE THEM FASTER AT THE SOURCE: no full rebuild or reload where a partial update works; reuse caches; rebuild only what changed; pre-compile the other tiers' shader variants in idle time or with renderer.compileAsync (KHR_parallel_shader_compile where available); spread unavoidable heavy work across frames so the page never freezes; target at least 2x faster graphics-mode switching than the base on the phone profile, with identical visual results and no leaks (10 switches back and forth: no heap growth, no duplicated objects or listeners). (2b) PRIOR WORK YOU MAY REUSE: the same paused WIP 637aa19 (origin/ui/seat-hands) also starts the owner's 2026-10-27 ask 'make it quicker to load the graphics settings' (handed to this lane by the session that owned it, 03:10 UTC): Roads.setQuality (a preset change rebuilds no road chunks; update() drops chunks beyond the draw distance and streams in the new ones), Terrain.setQuality (when q.props changes, tiles are marked stale by a generation counter and rebuilt nearest first within update()'s budget, each swapped only when its replacement is built so the world never empties), Game.applyQuality calling those instead of rebuilding, and a settings-speed check in tests/regression.mjs. It was cut off before any timing or review: MEASURE FIRST, cherry-pick or adapt what holds up, and say what you took. (3) A LOADING OVERLAY WITH A STATUS BAR: it appears only when an apply will take noticeable time (measured or predicted over ~250 ms), says what is happening in plain words (e.g. 'Rebuilding shadows  3 of 5'), and its bar fills from REAL progress (completed stages or work units, monotonic, never a fake timer); the game is paused safely underneath (or the apply waits for a safe moment) and resumes cleanly; tapping again during an apply is handled (queued or ignored, never a broken state); accessible (aria-live status, keyboard focus kept, reduced motion: no animated shimmer); in the style guide's tokens (PROJECT_OC_STYLE_GUIDE.md), readable on a phone. Build it as a shared component so the venues' own quality switches can use it later (do NOT edit venue files in this lane: src/onfoot/**). (4) ADD a regression check: a graphics-tier switch finishes within a budget on the test machine, the overlay's progress is monotonic and reaches 100 % then hides, and 10 switches leave no heap growth. Avoid files other lanes are changing: src/preview/cockpit.ts and src/preview/wheel-sport.ts (the dashboard/wheel lane), src/game/drivers.ts and src/onfoot/** (the characters lane), and the other session's files except as allowed in (5b) (never src/onfoot/people/*, src/preview/car-wheel.ts, src/game/vehicle/Physics.ts, src/preview/spec.ts). Our own brands; honest labels stay. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (one owner-test mark); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,modes and the new check; a BEFORE/AFTER timing table (phone profile and desktop) in the progress entry; frames of the overlay mid-switch at 390x844 and 1450x767 and of the settled result before/after (pixel-compare the settled frames) into tests/out/fast-settings/. ALSO (THE OWNER, 2026-11-11 ~7 PM PT, with a phone screenshot of v15 in the OC Hypercar's seat view: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/seat-view-v15-phone.webp, 969x547 landscape, 56 fps; look at it first): "graphics are still looking chopped there ... fix that". In that frame: the cockpit, the arms and the wheel look low-detail and jagged (the phone tier: Game.ts picks the car's 'phone' quality unless the setting is high/ultra), the image looks soft, and the THRUST panel and the THRUST / FOCUS TIME buttons sit in the middle over the wheel and the cluster. (5) SHARPER SEAT VIEW ON PHONES: find why it looks 'chopped' (render scale or pixel ratio, antialiasing, texture size and anisotropy, the phone-tier meshes of the cockpit and wheel, shadows) and fix it at the source: pick the default quality per device from a short measured warm-up (capable phones get HD; keep a real Low), dynamic resolution that holds ~60 fps instead of a permanently low scale, proper antialiasing for the cockpit (MSAA where available, else FXAA/SMAA), anisotropic filtering on the cockpit and road textures, smooth normals and enough segments on the phone-tier cockpit and wheel meshes that silhouettes don't look faceted; measure before/after on the phone profile (CDP CPU throttle 4) with the frame-time table (p95 no worse than +10 %). (5b) THE ARMS AND HANDS (src/preview/hands*): the session that owns them ALLOWED this lane to change them (its message, 2026-11-12 03:05 UTC) under these rules: put the smoothing in the geometry (hands-acc.ts for the sleeves and cuffs; hands-geo.ts or the arm builder for segment counts and smooth normals), phone tier first; keep the public API (buildDriverArms options, setTone, setWheelAngle(rad, dt)), the grip and thumb solve in hands-sdf.ts (the owner's thumbs fix) and the per-frame cost the same; measure triangles and draw calls before and after at seat view 1280x720 and 393x852 on phone and high; prove it with the seat views on test-hands.ts (?frame=game) before and after, plus the abilities group (the off-wheel poses) and the render and launch groups. The dark patches on the sleeves are most likely the shadow map's texels (wider than a finger): that session's paused, unjudged WIP commit 637aa19 on origin/ui/seat-hands (based on 1c3b943) addresses it (receiveShadow off for the arms; a cheap per-arm sun-visibility shade in a new src/preview/hands-sun.ts with sunPoints and setSunVisibility(v) on the arms API; small edits in hands.ts, hands-skin.ts and cockpit.ts): cherry-pick it ('git fetch origin ui/seat-hands') and adapt it to this cockpit.ts, or leave it and only smooth, and say which. Record what you changed in hands* precisely in the progress entry (the owner session will rebase its branch onto this). (6) THE HUD IN THE SEAT VIEW: on phones (969x547, 844x390 landscape and 390x844 portrait) the Thrust panel, the ability buttons and any other HUD box must never cover the wheel's centre or the instrument cluster in the seat view: move them to the sides/bottom corners in the seat view (other cameras keep today's layout), with the nav-hud overlap check extended to the seat view. Frames: the owner's view reproduced (OC Hypercar, seat view, 969x547 phone landscape, DPR 3) BEFORE and AFTER, plus 390x844 and 1280x720. (7) THE TOUCH CONTROLS (THE OWNER, 2026-11-11 ~10:35 PM PT, with an iPhone screenshot of v15 in portrait: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/owner/touch-controls-v15-phone.png; look at it first): "Let's make the brake button and gas and other buttons more sleek and bold and high tech". Restyle the on-screen GAS and BRAKE pedals, the STEER slider, the THRUST / ability hex buttons and the pause and rail buttons (src/ui/Touch.tsx and styles.css; HUD.tsx where needed): sleek, bold and high-tech in the game's own style guide tokens (dark glass panels, crisp lit edges and accent lines, clear bold glyphs and type, a satisfying pressed state with a quick glow and travel, haptics via navigator.vibrate where available and allowed), large hit targets (at least 48 px), never covering the wheel's centre or the cluster in the seat view (see 6), working in portrait (390x844, the owner's iPhone) and landscape (844x390, 969x547), left or right hands as today, reduced motion respected; input latency and behaviour unchanged (steering curve, pedal response, multi-touch). Frames BEFORE/AFTER of the owner's view (OC Hypercar, seat view, 390x844 portrait DPR 3 with the touch controls showing) and 844x390 landscape, plus the pressed states. (7b) THE THRUST CONTROLS (THE OWNER, ~10:40 PM PT): "Also make the thrust button less clustered": in the screenshot the THRUST panel (percentage bar, GROUND LOCK, HOP: CHARGING) sits stacked right on top of the THRUST and CLEAR PATH hex buttons and over the wheel. Declutter it: one clean Thrust control with the tank shown compactly on or around the button itself (a ring or slim bar) and its state in one short word, the ability button set apart with clear spacing, nothing overlapping, the wheel and cluster clear; same functions (hold to thrust, hop, ground lock state) and the same honest labels.
